ing: or pancetta, cut into small strips
st: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it well.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, Parmesan and [[1 tsp]] pepper into a thick paste. The eggs stay uncooked at this point and are cooked by the hot pasta.
Put the guanciale in a cold skillet and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the fat melts and the pieces are crisp.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook for 9 to 10 minutes until al dente.
Scoop out [[1 cup]] of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Turn off the heat under the skillet. Add the pasta and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and toss in the guanciale fat.
Move the pasta to the egg bowl, or let the pan cool for 1 minute. Add [[0.25 cup]] pasta water and toss fast so the sauce turns creamy and does not scramble.
Add more pasta water a splash at a time until glossy. Serve right away with extra cheese.

ing: 14 oz, drained and crushed by hand
torn into pieces and patted dry
st: Mix the flour, yeast, [[1 tsp]] salt and sugar. Add the water and [[1 tbsp]] oil and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 8 minutes on a floured counter until smooth and springy.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Put a pizza stone or an upside-down baking sheet in the oven. Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C) for 30 minutes.
Mix the crushed tomatoes with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Divide the dough in 2 and stretch each piece by hand into a 10 to 12 inch round on parchment paper.
Spread the sauce thinly, leaving a border, and scatter the mozzarella over it.
Slide onto the hot stone and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese is bubbling.
Top with the basil leaves and serve right away.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beef and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes and pepper. Simmer for 40 minutes on low.
Cook the noodles in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the pack says. Drain and lay flat.
For the bechamel, melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Cook for 6 minutes until thick. Add nutmeg and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a 9 by 13 inch dish.
Layer noodles, meat sauce, bechamel and a sprinkle of Parmesan. Repeat 3 times, finishing with bechamel, mozzarella and [[0.25 cup]] Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.
Keep the broth hot in a pot on low heat. Crumble the saffron into a ladle of broth and let it steep for 10 minutes.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and clear.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look glassy at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed. For no alcohol, use broth.
Add a ladle of broth and stir until nearly absorbed. Repeat, one ladle at a time, for about 18 minutes.
Add the saffron broth in the last 5 minutes. The rice should be creamy and tender with a slight bite.
Remove from heat. Stir in the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and the Parmesan hard for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper, rest for 2 minutes, and serve right away.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it well.
Cook the fettuccine for 9 to 10 minutes until al dente.
Scoop out [[1 cup]] of the pasta water, then drain.
Melt half the butter in a large wide pan over low heat. Add the garlic for 30 seconds if using.
Add the hot pasta and [[0.5 cup]] of the pasta water to the pan.
Add the remaining butter and the Parmesan a handful at a time, tossing constantly with tongs until a creamy sauce coats the noodles.
Add more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks thick.
Season with pepper and nutmeg, and serve right away.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Tie kitchen twine around each shank so the meat holds together. Season with salt and pepper and dredge in flour.
Heat the oil and butter in a Dutch oven. Brown the shanks for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion, carrots and celery for 8 minutes. Add [[2 clove]] of the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Boil for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and broth and return the shanks to the pot, standing upright so the marrow stays in.
Cover and braise in the oven for 2 hours until the meat is very tender and nearly falling off the bone.
Mix the parsley, lemon zest and the remaining garlic clove, minced, for the gremolata.
Skim the fat from the sauce, spoon it over the shanks, and top with the gremolata. Serve with risotto or polenta.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the zucchini and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the tomatoes, broth, salt, pepper and the Parmesan rind.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes with the lid half on.
Add the beans and pasta and cook for 10 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Remove the rind, taste, and adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with basil, a drizzle of olive oil and grated Parmesan.

ing: about 1 inch thick, such as ciabatta
st: Mix the tomatoes, minced garlic, basil, [[2 tbsp]] oil, vinegar, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Let the tomato mixture sit for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Heat the broiler or a grill pan to high.
Brush the bread slices with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Toast the bread for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp at the edges.
While the bread is hot, rub one side of each slice with the cut side of a whole garlic clove.
Spoon the tomato mixture over the bread just before serving.
Set a heatproof bowl over a pot of simmering water. Whisk the egg yolks and sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until pale, thick and 160°F (71°C), which cooks the eggs safely.
Take the bowl off the heat and whisk for 2 minutes until cooled slightly. Fold in the mascarpone until smooth.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks in another bowl and fold it into the mascarpone mixture.
Mix the coffee and marsala in a shallow dish.
Dip each ladyfinger into the coffee for 1 second per side. Do not soak them or they will fall apart.
Arrange half the dipped ladyfingers in a 9 by 9 inch dish, then spread half the cream on top.
Repeat with a second layer of ladyfingers and cream. Smooth the top.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Dust with cocoa powder just before serving.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until pale gold. Cool them.
Wash and dry the basil leaves very well, so the pesto does not turn watery.
Add the garlic, pine nuts and a pinch of salt to a food processor or mortar and grind to a rough paste.
Add the basil in two batches and pulse or pound until finely chopped.
With the machine running, slowly pour in the oil until the sauce looks creamy.
Stir in the Parmesan and Pecorino by hand. Taste and add salt if needed.
Toss with hot pasta, loosening with a spoon of pasta water, or store under a thin layer of oil in the fridge.
Crush the tomatoes with your hands or a fork in a bowl, keeping their juices.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant but not brown.
Stir in the oregano and red pepper flakes for 20 seconds.
Pour in the tomatoes with their juices, then add the salt and sugar.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened.
Stir in the basil and taste for salt.
Use over pasta, pizza or with meatballs.
Stir the flour, yeast, salt and sugar. Add the water and [[2 tbsp]] oil and mix into a wet, sticky dough.
Cover and let rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Pour [[0.25 cup]] oil into a 9 by 13 inch pan. Scrape the dough in and turn it once to coat.
Stretch the dough toward the corners. If it springs back, rest for 10 minutes and try again.
Cover and let rise for 45 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Dimple the dough all over with oiled fingers.
Drizzle with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil and sprinkle with rosemary and flaky salt.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool for 10 minutes in the pan before slicing.
Take the cheeses out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Cold cheese tastes flat and hard, so this step matters more than any other.
Pull the prosciutto slices apart gently one by one and drape them in loose ribbons across the board. Do not stack them flat or they stick together.
Fold each salame slice in half, then in half again into quarter fans. Roll the mortadella slices into loose cigars and set them in a row.
Break the Parmigiano into rough chunks with a short knife, working it open along the grain rather than cutting. Cut the pecorino into thin triangles.
Tear the mozzarella into pieces into a small bowl, or set the burrata whole. Put the olives in another small bowl and place both on the board.
Drizzle [[3 tbsp]] honey over the pecorino just before serving, or set it in a small pot with a spoon.
Add the focaccia squares and grissini in a bunch at one end, then fill the last gaps with the fig halves. Serve within an hour.
nt: Don't cook: slice, fold, arrange; cheeses at room temperature 30 minutes
Best swap: speck or bresaola for the mortadella and Grana Padano for Parmigiano; vegetarians skip the meat and add grilled artichokes and roasted peppers.

st: The night before, mix [[0.5 cup]] of the flour, [[0.5 cup]] water and a pinch of the yeast in a bowl. Cover and leave at room temperature for 12 hours until bubbly. This is the biga starter.
Add the remaining [[2.5 cup]] flour, [[1 cup]] water, [[0.5 tsp]] yeast, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil. Beat with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes until a very sticky, stretchy dough forms.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise for 1 hour. Fold it over itself 4 times with wet hands, then rest another 1 hour until doubled and full of bubbles.
Heavily flour a counter and tip the dough out gently to keep the air in. Cut it in half and stretch each piece into a rough rectangle about 10 by 4 inches.
Move the loaves to a floured towel or parchment. Dust the tops and rest 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 450°F with a baking sheet inside.
Slide the loaves onto the hot sheet and bake 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden and hollow sounding when tapped underneath.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes so the crumb sets.
nt: Baked at 450°F on a hot sheet
Best swap: all-purpose flour works for bread flour, but use 2 tbsp less water per loaf.

st: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Toast [[1 cup]] almonds on a tray for 8 minutes, cool, then roughly chop.
Whisk [[2 cups]] flour, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] baking powder and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Beat the 2 eggs with [[1 tsp]] orange zest and [[1 tsp]] vanilla. Pour into the flour and mix until a sticky dough forms, then knead in the almonds.
With floured hands, divide the dough in two and shape each into a log about 12 inches long and 2 inches wide. Place them on the sheet and brush with the beaten yolk.
Bake the logs 25 minutes until golden and firm. Cool for 15 minutes on the sheet.
Lower the oven to 300°F. Slice the logs on a diagonal into slices 0.5 inch thick with a serrated knife.
Lay the slices cut side down and bake 10 minutes, flip and bake 10 minutes more until dry and crisp. They harden further as they cool.
nt: Baked twice at 350°F then 300°F
Best swap: hazelnuts or pistachios for the almonds, same weight, or skip the nuts and add 1 cup dark chocolate chunks.

st: Pour [[3 tbsp]] of the cold milk into a small bowl, sprinkle in the gelatin and leave it for 5 minutes until it looks like soft applesauce.
Heat the cream, remaining milk, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and the vanilla seeds and pod in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming. Do not let it boil.
Take the pan off the heat, remove the pod, then whisk in the softened gelatin for 1 minute until no grains remain.
Pour the mixture through a sieve into a jug, then divide among six lightly oiled ramekins or glasses.
Cool on the counter for 20 minutes, cover loosely, then chill for at least 4 hours until set with a gentle wobble.
Simmer the strawberries with [[1 tbsp]] sugar and the lemon juice for 6 minutes until syrupy, then cool.
Dip each ramekin in hot water for 5 seconds, turn out onto a plate and spoon the berry sauce over the top.
nt: Chilled, no baking
Best swap: coconut cream and agar for a dairy-free version, use 1 tsp agar powder per 2 cups liquid.

st: Pile the flour on a board, make a well and crack in the eggs. Beat with a fork, pulling in flour, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the pork over medium heat for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through to 160°F. Cool completely.
Grind or finely mince the pork with the prosciutto and mortadella. Mix with the Parmigiano and nutmeg into a thick paste.
Roll the dough very thin, you should see your hand through it. Cut into 1.5 inch squares and keep covered so they do not dry.
Put a hazelnut-size bit of filling in the center of each square. Fold into a triangle, pinch the edges, then wrap the corners around your finger and press the tips together.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and season with salt.
Drop in the tortellini and cook 4 minutes, until they float and the dough is tender.
Ladle into warm bowls with plenty of broth and extra Parmigiano.
nt: Boiled and served in simmering broth
Best swap: skip the mortadella and use extra prosciutto, or use ricotta and spinach filling for a meatless version.

st: Mix the semolina and flour, add the warm water and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in, about 20 minutes. Drain, mash dry and cool.
Mix the potato with the pecorino, mint and a pinch of salt. Cook the garlic in [[1 tbsp]] oil, stir in the crushed tomatoes and basil and simmer 15 minutes for the sauce.
Roll the dough 1/16 inch thin and cut 3.5 inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center. Fold the edge of the circle up and pleat it over itself in a diagonal braid, pinching as you go, to make a closed ear of wheat.
Boil the culurgiones in salted water for 5 minutes, until they float and the dough is tender.
Lift out gently, plate with the warm sauce, and finish with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and more pecorino.
nt: Boiled, then served with a simmered tomato sauce
Best swap: use Parmigiano or aged manchego in place of pecorino sardo, same amount.

st: Warm [[1 cup]] of the water with the sugar in a small pot over medium heat, stirring until every crystal dissolves, about 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon zest and let the syrup cool for 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining [[1 cup]] water and the lemon juice, then strain into a shallow metal pan or baking dish.
Freeze 1 hour, then scrape the frozen edges into the center with a fork. Repeat every 30 minutes until the whole pan is fluffy ice crystals.
Freeze 1 more hour if needed so it is firm but still scrapeable, then scrape one final time.
Spoon into chilled glasses, garnish with mint and serve right away, traditionally with a brioche.
nt: Don't cook: syrup then frozen and scraped
Best swap: use lime or blood orange juice in the same amount, or cut the sugar to [[0.5 cup]] for a tarter ice.

st: Wash all of the fruit under cold running water and dry it. Squeeze the lemon into a large bowl, about [[3 tbsp]] juice, and stir in [[3 tbsp]] sugar until it dissolves.
Peel and core the apples and pears, then cut them into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss them in the lemon syrup straight away so they stay white.
Cut the peaches into similar cubes after removing the stone. Peel and segment the oranges over the bowl so you capture the juices.
Halve or quarter the strawberries, and halve the grapes. Add them to the bowl with the other fruit.
Add [[2 tbsp]] maraschino liqueur if using, and stir gently with a large spoon so the pieces keep their shape.
Cover the bowl and chill for at least 1 hour, stirring once, so the fruit releases juice and makes a light syrup.
Taste and add a little more sugar if needed. Serve in glasses topped with torn mint leaves.
nt: Don't cook: cut and macerate
Best swap: fresh orange juice and a little honey for the liqueur, and nectarines for peaches.

st: Heat the broiler to its highest setting with a rack 4 inches from the heat. Broil the whole peppers on a foil lined sheet for 15 to 18 minutes, turning, until blackened all over.
Put the hot peppers in a bowl and cover tightly for 15 minutes so the skins loosen. Peel, seed and tear into wide strips.
Toss the pepper strips with the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, the balsamic and salt. Marinate at least 10 minutes.
Toss the mozzarella with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil, torn basil, black pepper and the tomatoes in a bowl.
On a large board arrange the prosciutto in folds, the salami fanned out, the peppers, artichokes, mozzarella, olives and pepperoncini in separate groups.
Drizzle the remaining [[1 tbsp]] olive oil over the mozzarella and serve with the bread at room temperature.
nt: Peppers charred under the broiler or on a grill; all else is cured, marinated or fresh
Best swap: roasted mushrooms or marinated eggplant in place of the cured meats for a vegetarian board.

ing: sheep milk if possible, drained overnight
st: Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa, a pinch of salt and butter until crumbly. Add the Marsala to make a stiff dough, knead 5 minutes, wrap and rest 1 hour.
Beat the drained ricotta with [[0.75 cup]] powdered sugar until smooth. Fold in chocolate chips and orange peel. Chill.
Roll the dough very thin, 1/16 inch, and cut 4 inch rounds. Wrap each round around a metal cannoli tube and seal the overlap with a dab of water.
Heat the oil to 350°F in a deep pot. Fry 2 or 3 tubes at a time for 1 to 2 minutes until blistered and golden.
Drain on paper towels. When cool enough to handle, slide the shells off the tubes and cool completely.
Pipe the chilled filling into each shell just before serving, so the shells stay crisp. Dust with powdered sugar.
nt: Deep fried at 350°F
Best swap: use dry red or white wine for Marsala at the same amount, or bake the shells wrapped round foil tubes at 375°F for 12 minutes.

st: Tear the bread into 1 inch pieces. If it is fresh, dry it in a 300°F oven for 10 minutes. It should be firm but not browned.
Slice the onion thinly and soak it in cold water with a splash of vinegar for 10 minutes to mellow it, then drain.
Salt the tomato chunks in a large bowl and let them sit for 10 minutes so they release their juices.
Add the bread, cucumber and onion to the tomatoes and pour over [[0.33 cup]] olive oil and [[2 tbsp]] red wine vinegar.
Toss well, tear in the basil and let stand 15 minutes so the bread soaks up the juices. Taste and add salt if needed.
nt: Don't cook, bread optionally dried in the oven
Best swap: gluten-free sourdough or day-old focaccia in the same weight for the bread.

st: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook 1 minute, then stir in the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Mash half the beans with a fork. Add all the beans, the kale, stock and salt to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 40 minutes until the kale is very tender and the soup is thick.
Remove the rosemary. Stir in the bread chunks and let them soak for 10 minutes off the heat, then stir hard so the bread breaks up into the soup.
Ladle into bowls and finish with a generous thread of olive oil. It tastes even better reheated the next day.
nt: Simmered, then rested with bread
Best swap: use savoy cabbage or chard in place of lacinato kale; day-old sourdough works for the bread.

st: Heat the oven to 340°F. Grease a 9 inch round pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Melt the chocolate gently in a bowl over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Beat the butter with [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then stir in the cooled chocolate until fully combined.
Fold in the almond flour until no dry streaks remain.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt to soft peaks, then add the remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar and whip to stiff peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter to loosen it, then fold in the rest gently.
Pour into the pan and bake for 40 minutes until the top is cracked and a skewer comes out with moist crumbs. Cool in the pan, then dust with powdered sugar.
nt: Baked at 340°F
Best swap: ground hazelnuts or walnuts in equal amounts for the almond flour.

st: Heat the oven to 300°F and line two trays with parchment.
Whisk the almond flour, [[1 cup]] powdered sugar and baking powder in a bowl.
Whip the egg whites in a clean bowl for 3 minutes until stiff peaks form. The whites bake fully in the oven.
Fold the whites, almond extract and orange zest into the almond mix to make a sticky dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Dust your hands with powdered sugar and shape the dough into 2 inch ovals about 1/2 inch thick.
Place on the trays, dust the tops with plenty of powdered sugar and let them stand for 15 minutes.
Bake for 20 minutes until the surface cracks but the cookies stay pale. Cool on the tray; they firm as they cool.
nt: Baked at 300°F
Best swap: use pure almond extract at 1 tsp for bitter almond extract; blanched ground hazelnuts replace almond flour 1 to 1.

st: Stir the yeast and [[2 tbsp]] of the sugar into the warm milk. Let it sit for 10 minutes until foamy on top.

In a stand mixer with the dough hook, combine the flour, remaining [[6 tbsp]] sugar, salt, zest, vanilla, eggs, yolks and the foamy milk. Knead on medium for 10 minutes until a sticky, stretchy dough forms.
Add the butter [[1 tbsp]] at a time, waiting until each piece disappears. Keep kneading for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and shiny and pulls from the bowl sides.
Knead in the raisins and orange peel on low for 1 minute. Cover the bowl and let the dough rise somewhere warm for 2 hours until doubled.

Butter a 7 inch round cake pan and line the sides with a 5 inch tall collar of buttered parchment. Shape the dough into a tight ball, set it in the pan, cover, and let it rise 1 to 1.5 hours until it reaches the top of the pan.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Cut a shallow cross in the top and bake for 45 to 50 minutes. Tent with foil after 25 minutes once the top is deep gold. It is done at 195°F inside.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes, then lift out and cool fully on a rack before slicing, so the crumb sets.
nt: Enriched yeast dough, slow rise, baked at 350°F
Best swap: chopped dried apricots or dried cherries for the candied orange peel at the same amount.

ing: Barolo or other dry red wine
st: The night before, put the beef, wine, carrot, celery, onion, garlic, bay, rosemary and cloves in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours, turning once.
Lift the beef out and pat very dry. Strain the wine, keeping the vegetables and the liquid separate. Season the beef with salt.
Heat the butter and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the beef 4 minutes per side until dark brown all over, then set aside.
Add the drained vegetables to the pot and cook 8 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Return the beef, add the wine and [[1 cup]] broth. Bring to a bare simmer, cover and braise in a 300°F oven for 3 hours, turning the meat every hour, until a knife slides in easily.
Move the beef to a board and cover with foil. Blend or mash the vegetables into the liquid, then simmer 10 minutes to a sauce that coats a spoon.
Slice the beef against the grain, spoon over the sauce and serve with polenta or mashed potatoes.
nt: Marinated overnight, seared, then braised in the oven
Best swap: any dry, tannic red such as Nebbiolo, Cabernet or Chianti works if Barolo is too pricey, use 3 cups.

st: Chill a small martini or coupe glass in the freezer for 5 minutes.
Pull a fresh double espresso, about [[2 fl oz]], straight into a cocktail shaker.
Stir in [[2 tsp]] sugar while the espresso is hot so it dissolves fully.
Add [[1 cup]] ice cubes to the shaker and close the lid tightly.
Shake very hard for 15 to 20 seconds until the outside of the shaker is frosty. This creates the thick foam.
Strain into the chilled glass, keeping the ice back, so the coffee is topped with a pale cream. Serve immediately.
nt: Brewed hot, then shaken over ice
Best swap: [[2 fl oz]] very strong moka pot coffee or 2 tbsp instant espresso in hot water, in place of the espresso.

st: Bring [[4 l]] of water to a boil with the salt. Use a wide pot so the pasta stays submerged and cooks evenly.
Toast the cracked pepper in a large dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute. Turn off the heat.
Boil the pasta 2 minutes short of the package time. Scoop out [[1.5 cup]] of the starchy cooking water before draining.
Add [[0.5 cup]] pasta water to the pepper and bring to a simmer. Add the drained pasta and toss for 1 minute over medium heat.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 30 seconds. This stops the cheese from clumping into strings.
Add the pecorino in three handfuls, tossing hard and adding splashes of pasta water until you get a glossy, creamy sauce that coats the pasta.
Serve at once on warm plates with extra pepper and cheese on top.
nt: Boiled pasta, emulsified off the heat
Best swap: parmesan can replace up to half the pecorino for a milder sauce, but keep the pecorino for the real flavor.

ing: about 1.5 lb total, cut in 1 inch cubes
st: Toss the eggplant cubes with [[1 tsp]] salt in a colander and let them drain for 20 minutes. Pat dry with a towel.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplant in two batches until deep golden on all sides, about 6 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels.
In the same pan over medium heat, cook the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the crushed tomatoes and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
Boil the pasta in well salted water until al dente. Save a mug of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with half the eggplant and half the basil, adding splashes of pasta water to loosen it.
Plate and top with the remaining eggplant, the grated ricotta salata and more basil.
nt: Eggplant shallow fried, sauce simmered
Best swap: oven roast the eggplant at 425°F for 25 minutes with less oil, and use feta if you cannot find ricotta salata.

st: Cut all vegetables into bite-sized pieces. Place them in a bowl, toss with [[2 tbsp]] salt and cover with cold water. Leave 8 hours or overnight.
Drain and rinse the vegetables well, then drain again and pat them dry with a towel.
Bring [[2 cups]] vinegar, [[1 cup]] water, [[1 tbsp]] salt, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, peppercorns, bay leaves and garlic to a boil in a pot.
Add the vegetables and cook for exactly 2 minutes, just to take off the raw edge. They should stay crisp.
Pack vegetables into clean jars, pour the hot brine over to cover, and tap out air bubbles.
Cool to room temperature, seal and refrigerate. Eat after 3 days, and keep up to 1 month.
nt: Brined overnight then quick pickled; chill 3 days before serving
Best swap: apple cider vinegar for white wine vinegar at the same amount, or add olive oil on top for the Italian oil-cured style.

st: Stir [[4 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] yeast and [[1.75 cup]] cool water in a large bowl until no dry flour is left. The dough will be very wet. Rest 20 minutes, then mix in [[2 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 10 hours or overnight. The long cold rise gives the open, airy crumb that defines this pizza.
Heat the oven to 475°F with a rack in the lower third. Oil a 13 by 18 inch sheet pan with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Tip the cold dough into the pan and let it sit 30 minutes. Dimple and stretch it gently with oiled fingers to reach the corners.
Spread [[1 cup]] crushed tomatoes over the dough and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Bake 12 minutes until the edges are golden.
Scatter the torn mozzarella on top and bake 8 to 10 minutes more until the cheese bubbles and the bottom is crisp when lifted with a spatula.
Top with torn basil and drizzle with the last [[1 tbsp]] olive oil. Cut into rectangles with scissors or a sharp knife and serve warm.
nt: Baked at 475°F in a sheet pan
Best swap: use 00 flour or all-purpose flour 1 to 1 if you have no bread flour; the crumb is slightly less chewy.

st: Bring [[6 cup]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Whisk in the cornmeal in a thin steady stream so no lumps form. Lower the heat to a bare simmer.
Cook 35 to 40 minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon every few minutes, until thick and the grains are tender. Splash in hot water if it gets stiff.
Stir in [[4 tbsp]] butter until melted.
Fold in the fontina and [[0.5 cup]] Parmesan until stretchy and creamy. Season with pepper.
Serve hot in warm bowls with extra butter and cheese on top.
nt: Simmered slowly and stirred
Best swap: use instant polenta (5 minutes) if short on time, or Gruyere or mozzarella plus Parmesan for fontina.

ing: cuttlefish or squid, cleaned and chopped
st: Keep the stock at a low simmer in a pot beside the stove.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chopped cuttlefish and cook 5 minutes until opaque and slightly firm.
Add the rice and stir 2 minutes until the edges turn translucent. Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Dissolve the ink in a ladle of stock. Add it with one more ladle and stir. Keep adding stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente.
Off the heat, stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and the parsley. Season, cover and rest 2 minutes before serving.
nt: Toasted, then stirred with hot stock a ladle at a time
Best swap: use squid for cuttlefish; ink sachets are sold at fishmongers, use 1 sachet (4 g) per 1/2 cup rice.

ing: canned tuna in olive oil, drained
st: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes in a pot until fully hard set, cool in cold water, peel and chop them.
Flake the drained tuna in a bowl. Stir in [[4 tbsp]] mayonnaise, [[1 tbsp]] capers, [[1 tsp]] lemon juice and pepper.
Fold in the chopped egg and olives gently so the filling stays chunky.
Cut the crusts off every slice of bread with a bread knife.
Spread the filling thickly on 4 slices all the way to the edges. Cover with the other slices and press lightly.
Cut each sandwich diagonally into 2 triangles. Chill covered with a damp towel for 15 minutes before serving so they stay soft.
nt: Don't cook: just assemble, eggs boiled
Best swap: use mashed chickpeas with the mayonnaise for a tuna free filling. Use ham and mozzarella with a thin mayo layer as the other classic.

st: Pat all the seafood very dry with paper towels. Wet seafood spits and will not crisp.
Mix the all-purpose flour and semolina in a wide bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil to 375°F in a deep heavy pot. Test by dropping in a pinch of flour, which should sizzle at once.
Dredge a handful of seafood in the flour, shake off the extra and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until pale gold and crisp. Do not crowd the pot.
Lift out with a spider, drain on a rack and salt right away. Reheat the oil between batches.
Pile onto a platter with fried parsley and lemon wedges. Eat immediately.
nt: Deep fried in light flour dusting
Best swap: cauliflower florets and zucchini sticks for a mixed vegetable fritto; or use rice flour for gluten free.

st: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 6 minutes until soft.
Add the peppers and garlic with [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook 10 minutes, stirring, until the peppers start to wilt.
Stir in the tomatoes and capers. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook 5 more minutes until the juices are thick and the peppers are very tender.
Tear in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.
nt: Slowly stewed in a covered pan
Best swap: use a 14 oz can of diced tomatoes in place of fresh tomatoes.
